originals.title: How to reveal people’s preferences: Comparing time consistency and predictive power of multiple price list risk elicitation methods
originals.identity: Crossref agrees with own PMC XML front matter and body; print 2016, electronic 2017
originals.access: Complete primary main article XML recovered and inspected, including Appendix, 12 tables and 92 references; separate supplement not recovered
conditional_facts: Vienna N=96: nine incentivised MPL variants and two non-incentivised general/financial survey items in the same participants.

Sec3.2/Table5 directly tests inter-method rank correlations; Appendix/Table10 gives ordinary correlations. This is separate from three randomly repeated tasks over about 30 minutes and prediction of two investment implementations plus an auction.

Most between-method associations are low under conservative significance threshold, but positive correlations include .33, .44, .39 and questionnaire–questionnaire .46; not universal zero correlation.
PGhigh performs best overall by authors’ stability/prediction criteria; not every method or individual comparison is unstable or null.

Current Slovak study empirically correlates three changed measures; its whole-sample REM1–REM2=.46, REM1–REM3=.03 and REM2–REM3=.19. Grouped citations and changed methods alone do not resolve the research relationship.
actual_gaps: Numerical MPL parameter grids and separate robustness supplement not independently inspected.
Literal table significance anomalies and narrative/table differences preserved without correction.
No Pedroni name/citation/cohort link in recovered XML; absence of a possible shared cohort is not proven without the other full sources.
